newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker chartering thin, rates flat to firmer.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker chartering thin, rates flat to firmer.

text.p: Despite continued strength in crude prices, freight rates across most regions were flat to only slight firmer with fresh chartering activity thinning towards the end of the week, traders said.
Demand for VLCC tonnage and above was thin with trade from UK/Cont transatlantic and from the Mideast to the Far East thin.
Premiums for Middle East to Japan voyages held steady at around W62.5, with trade west to the U.S. Gulf valued around W52.5 and W55 for trade to UK/Cont.
Levels for Singapore deliveries pegged around W57 but were expected to drift lower with trade in the direction thin.
However, while rates for modern vessels were steady, rates for older tonnage for voyages east were seen under prressure.

Brokers Galbraith said that with so few modern vessels available, charterers who might otherwise shy away from the plethora of "older ladies" were putting enormous pressure on them to accept lower rates for Red Sea and other Eastern discharge options.
They saw more modern ships available towards the end of the month but said these were likely to be snapped up by South Korean charterers for early November.

Suezmax tonnage continued to find work and premiums for trade from West Africa transatlantic edged around five points higher to W105 although most traders felt tight modern tonnage avails were the main catalyst behind the rise here too.

Around 20 vessels of one million barrels, totalling over 2.5 million tonnes, in addition to two VLCCs have been booked from West Africa to Europe and the Americas this week, brokers E.A. Gibson said in their weekly report.
Active Inter UK/Cont trade saw rates for Aframax tonnage around 2-1/2 points firmer at W105, while brisk trade in the Med pushed rates for cross Med voyages up five points to W100.
